title: You and Decisions
description: Find out what gets in your way most when you have to make a big decision.

questions.dec_1: When buying something expensive, I research for days and read hundreds of reviews until my head spins (analysis paralysis).
questions.dec_2: Even for personal matters, I have to ask many friends, 'What do you think I should do?'
questions.dec_3: I often make big decisions within minutes, guided only by how I feel in the moment.
questions.dec_4: I'm so afraid of making the wrong decision that I let the option expire.
questions.dec_5: I'll change my decision if an authority figure (a parent or boss) doubts it even slightly.
questions.dec_6: To me, a bad decision is much better than no decision at all.
questions.dec_7: After deciding something, I keep thinking, 'What if I had chosen the other one?'
questions.dec_8: I strongly avoid being the sole decision-maker in team projects.
questions.dec_9: I often rely on sudden gut feelings and ignore facts or logic that contradict them.
questions.dec_10: I make long pros-and-cons lists for almost every important choice in my life.
questions.dec_11: My decisions are often a compromise based on what my family or partner wants.
questions.dec_12: I'm easily swayed by discounts, limited-time offers, or urgent deals without thinking it through.
questions.dec_13: The thought that no decision is ever '100% perfect' really bothers and torments me.
questions.dec_14: If a decision turns out badly, I feel a little relieved if others agreed with the choice too (so it's not purely my fault).
questions.dec_15: When I'm upset or very stressed, I tend to take drastic steps like quitting suddenly or ending a relationship.
questions.dec_16: I struggle with simple decisions (like picking lunch) when there are too many options.
questions.dec_17: Getting most people's support is crucial before I dare to change direction.
questions.dec_18: I rarely make a backup plan; I jump straight into Plan A and hope everything works out.
questions.dec_19: I often stay up all night weighing two options that are actually both fine.
questions.dec_20: I often call my parents or best friend from a clothing store just to get approval before buying something.
questions.dec_21: As soon as a fresh idea pops into my head, I act on it right then without considering the money or energy needed.
questions.dec_22: I feel the information I have is never enough to make a solid final decision.
questions.dec_23: The weight of having free choice makes me wish someone older or smarter would take control of my life.
questions.dec_24: I tend to ignore warnings and advice from people close to me once I really want something.

results.description: You think through every worst-case scenario and research endlessly until you run out of time to choose.
You feel unsafe deciding on your own and need validation from ten different people before you move.
You hate waiting, so you just pick the fastest option to make the stress go away, without thinking about the consequences.
